title: Interpreting and Comparing Statistical Graphs
introduction: Consolidate primary mathematics and prepare for secondary study through interpreting and comparing statistical graphs.
definition: Choose graphs appropriate to the data: bar charts compare categories, line graphs show ordered changes, and pie charts show parts of a whole. Read scales, units and axis ranges carefully. A truncated axis can exaggerate visual differences.

visuals.label: 72° sector
visuals.alt: 72° sector — One fifth of a circle.

examples.question: A pie chart represents 240 pupils and one sector is 72°.

exercises.question: Sector of 90° represents what percent? Number only.
A chart represents 360 people; a 60° sector has how many?
Sales rise from 80 to 100. Increase percent?
A bar chart starts at 90 instead of zero. Can it exaggerate differences? yes/no

summary: Choose graphs appropriate to the data: bar charts compare categories, line graphs show ordered changes, and pie charts show parts of a whole. Read scales, units and axis ranges carefully. A truncated axis can exaggerate visual differences.
